context: `se trace` is implemented in SCRIPTS/se_core/commands.py (cmd_trace, _trace_failure, _trace_emit_failure, _build_reverse_targets, _context_reverse_closure, _resolve_kind), wired in SCRIPTS/se_core/cli.py and reporting.py (build_trace_envelope), and covered by TESTS/test_trace.py (19 tests). It walks the dependency graph between a project's records in either direction and is read-only by construction. The command was merged as a documented support subcommand: it is listed in DECLARED_SUPPORT of TESTS/test_cli_contract_boundary.py and in the support list of COMMANDS/README.md, so its interface, risk, permissions and limits are not contractual. ADR-0020 requires an ADR plus a VERSION bump to widen the contract.
problem: How can `se trace` be promoted into the command contract without ambiguity about its interface, risk, permissions and limits, and so that agents running through a generated adapter expose it as a real command instead of an undocumented CLI extra?

options_considered.option: Keep `trace` as declared support (no ADR, no VERSION bump)
pros: No contract change and no release ceremony
The implementation and tests stay untouched
Fast path while the command is still settling
cons: Interface, risk and permissions remain non-contractual
The generated adapters (OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex) do not expose it
The command is absent from the two summary tables and from the console's declared/implemented view
ADR-0020's contract rule is bypassed for a command that reads the whole record graph

options_considered.option: Promote `trace` to the command contract (ADR + minor bump + adapter + docs/tests)
pros: One governed surface: interface, risk, permissions and limits are explicit
The command already has execution and 19 tests
Removes `trace` from DECLARED_SUPPORT and fixes the CLI boundary
The OpenCode adapter and the human summary tables are regenerated from the contract
cons: Requires an ADR and a VERSION minor bump
commands.json, README, reference docs, boundary/summary/adapter tests and .opencode must be updated together

options_considered.option: Duplicate the command under a new name and leave `trace` as support
pros: No change to the existing support command
cons: Duplicates an implemented walker and its tests
Two tracing paths drift and split the evidence
Adds surface instead of governing the existing one

decision: `trace` becomes contract command CMD-0027 (name `trace`, agent `shema-ai-coordinador`, `execution_intent` ANALYZE, `risk_level` low, `gate` null, `mutates` false, `implemented` true, permissions [READ, ANALYZE]) and `COMMANDS/commands.json.interface_version` moves from 0.5.0 to 0.6.0. The coordinator is the assigned agent because the command only reads and analyses records, and both permissions are a subset of that agent's grants. Contractual semantics: (1) `se trace <record_id> --project <dir>` is read-only and never mutates the project; (2) `--direction forward|reverse|both` selects the traversal (default forward), `--depth` (default 3) and `--cap` (default 100) bound it, and a walk cut short is reported as `truncated` instead of silently dropped; (3) `--kind` disambiguates records that carry no identifier prefix (SDD, ODD, RDD, RUN); (4) `--json` emits a `se.trace/1` envelope, distinct from `se.report/1`, carrying root, direction, depth, cap, truncated, gaps, forward/reverse nodes and edges; (5) exit codes follow the global conventions: 0 success, 1 validation/usage failure of the target, 2 usage error; (6) unresolved references are reported as `gaps` rather than failing the walk.
reason: A single contractual surface prevents silent growth, and the command already exists, is tested and is read-only. Recording it in the contract makes its interface, risk and limits reviewable, exposes it through the generated adapters, and removes an entry from DECLARED_SUPPORT. The alternative of duplicating it would add surface instead of governing it.
consequences: COMMANDS/commands.json gains CMD-0027 and interface_version 0.6.0; COMMANDS/README.md and DOCS/reference/commands.md list 27 commands; TESTS/test_cli_contract_boundary.py removes `trace` from DECLARED_SUPPORT; TESTS/test_commands_summary_tables.py keeps both summary tables in sync; TESTS/test_opencode_adapter.py expectation counts grow by one generated command; `.opencode/commands/trace.md` is generated by `se adapter opencode`, never hand-written. VERSION moves 0.11.0 -> 0.12.0 (minor, backward-compatible new command) together with SYSTEM.json, MASTER SYSTEM/VERSION, the distribution manifest, `DOCS/reference/versioning.md`, the CHANGELOG entry and the coverage-baseline rebase. Declared limits, not hidden: the walk is bounded, so a dense graph yields a truncated (never complete) result; the reverse index is rebuilt per invocation and is not cached; the command reports gaps but does not repair references.
